## Purpose

This document is a topic of the SDBS project, recorded alongside the SDBS
index and the single-path artifact pipeline observation. The index describes
SDBS as a build system. The artifact pipeline observation describes the
production side: emulation, verification, robotics, and documentation
converge into one artifact pipeline. This document describes the consumption
side of the same system: what happens after SDBS publishes documents, and
how the corpus SDBS produces becomes knowledge that users, agents, and
machines can query.

The document records the domain boundary, the substrate stack, the
conceptual pipeline, the current state, the milestones, and the open
decisions. It intentionally omits code-level detail. A separate
specification will follow when development begins.

## The Domain

SDBS produces a corpus that is already structured for machine consumption: a
global index and per-document machine-readable pages, extracted as part of
every build. Today the corpus is a static artifact. **The vision is
knowledge-base-ization: the corpus SDBS publishes becomes a living knowledge
base that users, agents, and machines can query.**

SDBS is the entry point of the domain. The domain has SDBS and four
ecosystem roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
|------|----------------|
| SDBS, the corpus producer | Builds, validates, heals, and extracts the machine-readable corpus from source documents |
| Structural addressing | Gives every document and fact a structural coordinate, replacing hash-based identity |
| Materialization | Lands the coordinate space on media: file today, signal, network, and GPU later |
| Runtime | Holds the fact blackboard, accumulates verified facts, and enables graph traversal and gap detection |
| Client and edge | Runs the spatial state engine anywhere, desktop, mobile, or a pocket stick, with offline self-custody |

The two SDBS documents meet at the corpus. The artifact pipeline observation
describes how the corpus is produced; this document describes how it is
consumed as knowledge.

## The Substrate Stack

SDBS sits at the top of the stack as the knowledge-ization engine that turns
source documents into the corpus. Beneath it, the stack is layered, and each
layer has a single responsibility. Structural addressing (tagma) provides the
coordinate space in which every document and fact resides. Materialization
(chton) lands that space onto physical media, so the knowledge base persists
without a separate serialization step. The runtime (neXus) keeps facts
immutable and accumulating, carries the lifecycle of exploration, and
constrains admissible actions. The client sits at the edge and carries the
same spatial state engine to any device.

## The Conceptual Pipeline

Source documents follow a single conceptual path. The first three stages are
SDBS's own build stages; the last three carry the corpus into the knowledge
base.

| Stage | Role |
|-------|------|
| Validation and healing | Structural defects resolved before rendering |
| Rendering | Corpus built into published formats |
| Machine-readable extraction | Global index and per-document pages produced |
| Ingestion | Pages become facts with origins and coordinates |
| Indexing | Coordinate index and semantic index rebuilt |
| Query | Search, time-travel, and graph access over accumulated facts |

Beyond the full pipeline, SDBS supports a fast authoring loop: individual
documents can be previewed directly, and their published artifacts collected
for distribution. This loop keeps the corpus current between full builds and
connects to the artifact pipeline described in the sibling observation.

The pipeline is exercised end to end in minimal form today: the corpus SDBS
publishes is fetched, each page is stored as a fact, and coordinate and
semantic indexes are rebuilt. What exists today is the ingestion half. The
service surface and the refresh cadence form the remaining half.

## Why Now

SDBS already produces the corpus format that corresponds to a young standard
for LLM-readable documentation, and agent tooling increasingly consumes such
corpora directly. The reference deployment is live and already feeds the
ingestion path. The first production instantiation of the knowledge domain
is therefore not a plan; it is an operating capability with a known gap.

The timing is favorable for three reasons. The corpus standard is young
enough that early capability defines the conventions. The reference
deployment provides a continuous test corpus that grows with every SDBS
build. The client and edge layer already runs on the same engine, so
capability gained in this domain propagates to the edge by design of the
shared substrate.

## Current State

The boundary between verified facts and projections is explicit.

- SDBS produces the machine-readable corpus as part of every build of the
  reference documentation suite. Verified.
- A fast authoring loop previews individual documents and collects published
  artifacts as part of the command surface. Verified.
- The corpus is published and publicly fetchable. Verified.
- An ingestion path fetches the corpus and stores each page as a fact with
  coordinate and semantic indexing. Verified as existing capability.
- The service surface for normal users is a known gap. Verified as absent.
- Refresh is manual today; scheduled and diff-based refresh is absent.
  Verified as absent.
- Storage routing through the materialization layer is not yet adopted.
  Projected.
- The client and edge integration with the knowledge base is designed but
  not built. Projected.

## Milestones

Phase 1: Corpus service. The corpus SDBS publishes becomes queryable through
a persistent service with scheduled refresh and diff-based incremental
updates. The deliverable is a searchable knowledge base over the published
corpus. The evidence criterion is a running service that reflects corpus
changes without manual intervention.

Phase 2: Storage routing. The knowledge store adopts the materialization
layer as its persistence surface. Real workload then drives the
materialization layer's development: the file-origin layer, binding
strategies, and the key-value protocol are exercised by the corpus at scale.
The evidence criterion is a knowledge base that persists and restores
through the materialization surface.

Phase 3: Client integration. The client app surfaces the knowledge base as a
workspace with offline self-custody. The same spatial state engine that fits
in a pocket scales to the service. The evidence criterion is a multi-device
session that queries the knowledge base offline and synchronizes through the
shared substrate.

Phase 4: Scale and governance. Multiple corpora, teams, and agents join the
same knowledge base. Provenance and audit follow the runtime's governance
layer, and each deposit strengthens the shared primitives. The evidence
criterion is a corpus larger than the reference suite managed with the same
guarantees.

Development starts at Phase 1.

## Open Decisions

Four decisions are recorded for the development kickoff. Each is a decision
point, and this document does not settle them.

- Service surface: desktop application first, hosted endpoint first, or both.
- Refresh strategy: scheduled full sync versus diff-based incremental
  ingestion.
- Storage routing: adoption of the materialization layer at Phase 2 or
  earlier.
- Distribution and commercial boundary: package identity, open-core
  boundary, and the relationship to the client and edge product.

## Scope

This document is a topic of the SDBS project, not a specification. It does
not describe interfaces, formats, or implementation details. It does not
claim universal applicability. SDBS is one functional region of the shared
substrate, and its growth follows the ecosystem pattern: each deposit
strengthens the primitives for every other domain.
